analysis.title: US CPI acceleration points to risk of steeper tightening cycle
key_insights: October CPI showed broadening US inflation pressure: headline +0.4% m/m, core +0.3% m/m for the second month running.
3m annualised core CPI rose to 3.75% from 3.41% in September and 1.97% in August. Supercore (core services less shelter) rose 0.4% m/m, lifting its 3m annualised pace to 5.44%.
The rise in services inflation indicates inflation pressure is extending beyond energy and tariffs.

ANZ expects the Fed to raise rates 25bp in December and another 25bp in March. Risks are skewed toward more than the 75bp of tightening currently anticipated over the cycle, including September's 25bp hike. ANZ will re-examine its forecast path in the coming days.

ANZ says the Fed's decision to hold in October looks like a mistake in hindsight. If the Fed prefers to wait for more data, it may be prepared to raise in larger increments than 25bp when it does act.
Data since the October FOMC meeting has been consistently strong: Q3 GDP +3.4% saar, private domestic demand +4.9% saar (highest since mid-2021), October NFP +165k with the 3m average at 137k vs 79k.
The inflation acceleration coincides with firmer activity and labour market conditions, which ANZ reads as demand-led inflation.
Market-based core PCE rose 0.34% m/m in September. The 0.4% m/m rise in October supercore CPI points to firm October core PCE.

Chairman Warsh has given no forward guidance, and the Fed has departed from the historical pattern of tightening at sequential meetings early in a cycle, so the FOMC's short-term reaction function is hard to read. Warsh has said inflation is a choice and the FOMC will not tolerate persistently elevated inflation.

ANZ sees merit in Governor Waller's argument that rates may need to rise 50bp next month. Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed president Hammock, who both dissented in October, could plausibly support 50bp.
